films.title: You've Got Mail
films.note: Bookshops, brownstones and a meeting by the Hudson.

films.title: Anora
films.note: A search through the restaurants and streets of South Brooklyn.

films.title: When Harry Met Sally
films.note: Conversations over lunch and walks through Central Park.

films.title: Ghostbusters
films.note: A firehouse, a library and a very unusual apartment building.

films.title: Breakfast at Tiffany’s
films.note: Window-shopping on Fifth Avenue and an East Side brownstone.

films.title: Home Alone 2
films.note: Kevin’s first New York adventure, from the Plaza to the park.

films.title: Spider-Man
films.note: A city seen from the rooftops and the Roosevelt Island tram.

locations.name: 91st Street Garden
locations.visit_note: Use the park paths to reach the garden.

scenes.scene: Kathleen and Joe finally meet as their online selves in the riverside garden.

locations.name: Café Lalo
locations.visit_note: Café Lalo vacated this address in 2024. Visit the former filming location from the sidewalk.

scenes.scene: Kathleen waits with a book and a rose for her anonymous correspondent.

locations.name: The Shop Around the Corner
locations.visit_note: The fictional bookstore was created inside an existing shop. View the address from the sidewalk.

scenes.scene: The small shop used for Kathleen’s bookstore; it was never a real children’s bookstore.

locations.name: Kathleen’s brownstone
locations.visit_note: Stay on the public sidewalk; the residence is not a visitor attraction.

scenes.scene: The exterior used for Kathleen Kelly’s home.

locations.name: Zabar’s
locations.visit_note: Visit as a customer and check current hours.

scenes.scene: The grocery-store checkout scene brings Kathleen and Joe face to face.

locations.name: Verdi Square
locations.visit_note: A street-level stop near the subway entrances.

scenes.scene: The neighborhood square appears in the film’s Upper West Side streetscapes.

locations.name: Tatiana Restaurant & Nightclub
locations.visit_note: Check with the venue for dining and show access.

scenes.scene: Ani and the men look for Ivan at the boardwalk restaurant.

locations.name: Williams Candy
locations.visit_note: Visit during business hours; the shop is a working business.

scenes.scene: The search for Ivan erupts into a confrontation among the candy counters.

locations.name: Ocean View Cafe
locations.visit_note: Check current opening hours with the venue.

scenes.scene: During the search, a woman in the café suggests Ivan has been kidnapped.

locations.name: Parkview Diner
locations.visit_note: Visit as a customer; confirm current hours before making a special trip.

scenes.scene: The diner appears during the long search through South Brooklyn.

locations.name: Coney Island Boardwalk
locations.visit_note: The pin is a public access point for the broader filming area.

scenes.scene: The oceanfront boardwalk is one of the film’s South Brooklyn exterior locations.

locations.name: Katz’s Delicatessen
locations.visit_note: Visit as a customer; allow time for a queue.

scenes.scene: Harry and Sally’s famous lunchtime conversation unfolds at a deli table.

locations.name: Central Park Boathouse
locations.visit_note: The lakeside paths offer an outdoor stop; dining access is separate.

scenes.scene: Sally talks with her friends beside the lake at the Boathouse.

locations.name: The Metropolitan Museum of Art
locations.visit_note: Museum admission is required for the galleries. The pin marks the main entrance.

scenes.scene: Harry and Sally talk while walking through the museum’s Egyptian galleries.

locations.name: Bethesda Terrace
locations.visit_note: Reach the terrace from the park’s pedestrian paths.

scenes.scene: Bethesda Terrace and nearby paths appear during their Central Park walks.

locations.name: Hook & Ladder 8
locations.visit_note: Keep the firehouse entrance and vehicle access clear.

scenes.scene: The real firehouse supplies the headquarters exterior; the interior was filmed in Los Angeles.

locations.name: New York Public Library
locations.visit_note: Start at the Fifth Avenue entrance; check visitor access for interiors.

scenes.scene: The team investigates a ghost at the library in the opening sequence.

locations.name: Dana’s apartment building
locations.visit_note: View from the public sidewalk; the building is residential.

scenes.scene: Dana’s building exterior. The rooftop and destructive finale also relied on sets and effects.

locations.name: Tiffany & Co.
locations.visit_note: The exterior can be seen from Fifth Avenue.

scenes.scene: Holly stops at the windows with her breakfast in the opening scene.

locations.name: Holly Golightly’s brownstone
locations.visit_note: View from the sidewalk. Interior and fire-escape scenes used studio sets.

scenes.scene: The real exterior is number 169, although the film shows the number 167.

locations.name: The Plaza Hotel
locations.visit_note: The street exterior is the simplest stop; interior access depends on hotel policies.

scenes.scene: Kevin checks into the Plaza during his unplanned trip to New York.
Roger Thornhill’s mistaken-identity adventure begins at the Plaza.

locations.name: Gapstow Bridge & The Pond
locations.visit_note: The pin marks the bridge beside the pond.

scenes.scene: Kevin encounters the Pigeon Lady around the pond in Central Park.

locations.name: Rockefeller Center
locations.visit_note: The Christmas tree is seasonal; the plaza can be visited separately.

scenes.scene: Kevin reunites with his mother beneath the Christmas tree.

locations.name: Grand Central Terminal
locations.visit_note: Use the public concourse; follow station access rules.

scenes.scene: Thornhill makes his escape from New York through Grand Central.

locations.name: Roosevelt Island Tramway
locations.visit_note: The pin marks the Manhattan station. Riding requires a fare; check current service.

scenes.scene: The tramway is part of the Green Goblin’s climactic threat to Mary Jane and the passengers.

locations.name: Times Square
locations.visit_note: The pin marks the pedestrian area; the sequence also uses effects.

scenes.scene: The Green Goblin interrupts the World Unity Festival in Times Square.
